title: Team Structure & Delivery: Conway's Law to Platform Teams
summary: Quick revision notes on how team structure shapes architecture and delivery: Conway's law, team topologies, service ownership, monorepo vs polyrepo, independent pipelines, deployment frequency and platform teams.

chapters.title: Conway's Law and Team Topologies
points: Conway's law: a system's design mirrors the communication structure of the organisation that builds it
Inverse Conway manoeuvre: shape teams around the target architecture first, so the architecture follows
Four team types: stream-aligned (owns a flow of value), enabling (coaches others), complicated-subsystem (deep specialists), platform (provides self-service internals)
Three interaction modes: collaboration (temporary, high-bandwidth), X-as-a-Service (clear API, low contact), facilitating (coach and unblock)
Mistake: splitting teams by technical layer (UI/backend/DB) forces every feature to cross three teams and creates hand-offs

chapters.title: Service Ownership and Boundaries
points: You build it, you run it: the owning team handles design, deploy, on-call, incidents and cost for its service
One service has exactly one owning team; shared ownership means no ownership
Ownership artefacts: service catalogue entry, on-call rotation, runbook, SLOs, and a named contact
Team cognitive load limit: a team should own only as many services as it can fully understand and operate (about 1-3 typical)
Mistake: a shared database or shared library across teams creates hidden coupling, so a change needs cross-team coordination

chapters.title: Monorepo vs Polyrepo
points: Monorepo: many services in one repo; gives atomic cross-service commits, one dependency version set and easy refactors
Polyrepo: one repo per service; gives clear ownership, independent access control and release cadence, but cross-repo changes need coordinated PRs
Comparison row: monorepo shares code easily but needs scaling tooling; polyrepo isolates but risks version drift of shared libraries
Monorepo tooling: CODEOWNERS for per-path review, and affected-only builds with Bazel, Nx or Turborepo
Mistake: a monorepo without path-based CI runs every build for every change; a polyrepo without shared-library versioning drifts

chapters.title: Independent Pipelines per Service
points: Each service has its own build, test, deploy pipeline and can ship without releasing the others
Monorepo trigger: path filters, e.g. GitHub Actions `on: push: paths: ['services/orders/**']`, so only the changed service builds
Independent deploy needs backward-compatible APIs and contract tests (e.g. Pact) so consumers don't break
Use versioned artefacts (immutable image tag per commit SHA) and promote the same artefact through staging to prod
Mistake: a lockstep release train or one shared pipeline brings back a distributed monolith, where services must deploy together

chapters.title: Deployment Frequency and Platform Teams
points: DORA metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore service
Elite performers deploy on demand (many times a day) with a low change failure rate; small batches lower risk
Enablers of frequent deploys: trunk-based development, feature flags, automated tests, canary or blue-green rollout
Platform team: builds an internal developer platform (golden paths, CI/CD templates, self-service infra) and treats developers as customers
Mistake: a platform team acting as a ticket-queue gatekeeper, or mandating tools without being usable; measure adoption, not mandates

chapters.title: Team and Delivery Cheat Sheet
points: Conway's law: org structure becomes architecture; use the inverse Conway manoeuvre to design on purpose
Team types: stream-aligned, enabling, complicated-subsystem, platform; modes: collaboration, X-as-a-Service, facilitating
Ownership: one team per service, you build it you run it, with catalogue, on-call, runbook and SLOs
Repos: monorepo for atomic change and shared code, polyrepo for isolation; path filters and CODEOWNERS for monorepos
Delivery: independent pipeline per service, contract tests, immutable artefacts, track the 4 DORA metrics, platform team offers self-service golden paths
